records.description: A provider-issued product ID exists on the offer, but it is scoped to that single provider/listing — it must never be treated as a universal identity that would justify matching it against a DIFFERENT retailer's product ID for the 'same' item.
records.notes: types/canonicalDressingRoomItem.ts:26-41 CanonicalPurchaseOption.productId; supabase/functions/scan-identify/canonicalCommerce.ts:23 CanonicalOffer.providerProductId. Both are provider/offer-scoped identifiers, not universal product codes — there is no evidence in source that the same physical product carries the same productId across two different retailers' listings.

records.description: An offer with no productId, no SKU, and no other identity field at all — this must be handled as 'no stable identity', not silently treated as identical to any other offer with the same title/brand.
records.notes: services/dressingRoomCommerce.ts optionFingerprint (~line 174-183) falls back to an empty string for a missing productId component, which is a real, deliberate 'no stronger signal available' state in the current dedup fingerprint — not an error.

records.description: SKU, GTIN, UPC, and EAN fields do not exist anywhere in this app's real production commerce types. This fixture documents that absence explicitly so the corpus does not silently invent these fields elsewhere.

input.note: no input record — this documents an absence, not a value

records.notes: Confirmed absent across RecommendedProduct, CanonicalOffer/CanonicalProduct, CanonicalPurchaseOption, PurchaseOption/WatchCandidate, ProductMatch during the shape census. The only place these field names appear in this repository is the RESEARCH/PROPOSAL shape tools/canonical-product-identity/lib/offerFactory.js:16-46 (RetailOffer), which is explicitly a design lab artifact, not shipped production schema — Section 7 'reuse pattern, not implementation' applies: this corpus does not adopt that invented shape as if it were real.

records.description: No field in production source establishes a governed, stable identity that is comparable ACROSS retailers for the same physical product. This is the single most important input to the Grouping Readiness verdict.

records.notes: supabase/functions/scan-identify/canonicalCommerce.ts:133-141 canonicalProductKey deliberately excludes retailer/source from its key so that same-product-different-retailer listings CAN collapse together — but it does so via fuzzy title-token matching, not an exact governed ID, and supabase/functions/scan-identify/watchlistCapability.ts:9-11 explicitly documents that this same function 'groups colorways together and is unstable under a retailer re-title.'
